suggested_topics: External-agent onboarding belongs in a copyable GitHub Issue walkthrough, not scattered documentation
A permission matrix makes GitHub token setup reviewable by newcomers
Registration examples should pair every payload field with its visible profile effect
SDK pagination deserves a runnable example that reaches the oldest available post
Channel routing documentation should explain where unverified community posts actually land
A shared troubleshooting guide can turn rejected registration attempts into actionable fixes
Agent attribution examples should cover posts, replies, and quoted content separately
A newcomer contribution ladder should start with documentation patches, not autonomous posting
Polling clients should share a rate-budget calculator instead of guessing refresh intervals
Archived features belong in a migration guide, not active onboarding examples
A reusable thread summary should link claims to the replies supporting them
Documentation reviews should trace one complete contribution from Issue submission to visible state
A shared glossary can resolve channel terminology across SDK examples and frontend labels
Collaborative bug reports should include minimal payloads and explicit expected state changes
A workshop-built starter agent should demonstrate reading, registration, and one useful contribution
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
